proposal.utterance: Classify 'agent connectedness' as a kind of entity.

entities.label: AgentConnectedness
entities.rationale: Agent connectedness is a property that inheres in agents (or collections of agents) — it characterizes the degree or mode of relational binding among agents. As a measurable, attributable property of a bearer rather than a process or information content, it fits best under Quality (BFO_0000019). It is not a Role (externally grounded social function) nor a Disposition (internally grounded capacity to act), but rather a quality capturing a structural-relational state of the bearer at a time.

relations.rationale: AgentConnectedness is proposed as a subclass of BFO Quality (BFO_0000019), since it represents an intrinsic relational property inhering in one or more agents.

open_questions: Is 'agent connectedness' intended as a dyadic relational quality between two specific agents, or a collective/network-level property inhering in a group of agents? This may affect whether it should be a Quality or a Disposition (if it is a latent capacity to form connections).

Is 'agent connectedness' meant to capture a social/institutional mode of bonding (possibly a subclass of existing working:RelationalCoherence or working:RelationalStructure), or is it a distinct psychological or physical property?
Should 'agent connectedness' be an individual (a specific named instance of connectedness) or a class (a kind of connectedness)? The utterance says 'a kind of entity', suggesting a class.
Is this concept intended to bear on legal agents specifically (e.g., parties to a contract, members of an institution), or on agents in general?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asks to classify 'agent connectedness' as a kind of entity, i.e., as a class. Agent connectedness most naturally denotes a relational property — a quality of how agents are bound or linked to one another — which in BFO 2020 is modeled as a Quality (BFO_0000019), a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer. It is not a Process (it does not unfold in time as a happening), not a Role (it is not an externally conferred social function), and not a Generically Dependent Continuant (it is not an information content that can be copied). The closest existing working classes are RelationalCoherence (BFO_0000019) and StructurallyGroundedIdentity (BFO_0000019), but 'agent connectedness' is sufficiently distinct in focus — emphasizing agent-to-agent binding rather than coherence of a structure or identity grounding — to warrant a new class. Open questions remain about whether it is dyadic or collective, and whether it applies specifically to legal agents.
